avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin D (>4000 IU daily long-term)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Tenofovir causes renal tubular dysfunction and hypophosphatemia; excessive vitamin D may compound electrolyte abnormalities and worsen renal impairment risk
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor vitamin D levels; limit supplementation to recommended dietary allowance (600-800 IU daily for most adults); assess for deficiency before supplementing

avoid_supplements.name: Nephrotoxic supplements (Aristolochic acid, high-dose NSAIDs)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive renal toxicity with tenofovir-induced nephrotoxicity; risk of acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease progression
avoid_supplements.action: Absolutely avoid; use acetaminophen for pain relief instead; if NSAIDs necessary, use lowest dose with adequate hydration and renal monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Phosphate binders (calcium carbonate, sevelamer)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Tenofovir causes hypophosphatemia; phosphate binders may further reduce phosphate absorption and exacerbate electrolyte depletion
caution_supplements.action: Use only if clinically indicated for hyperphosphatemia; monitor serum phosphate levels every 3-6 months

caution_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
caution_supplements.mechanism: May induce P-glycoprotein, potentially reducing tenofovir exposure, though clinical significance is minimal
caution_supplements.action: Counsel on alternative antidepressants; monitor viral load if concurrent use unavoidable

avoid_foods.name: High sodium foods (processed meats, canned soups, fast food)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium intake increases urinary phosphate wasting and may worsen tenofovir-associated renal tubular dysfunction and electrolyte abnormalities
avoid_foods.action: Counsel on DASH diet principles; limit sodium to <2300 mg daily; monitor blood pressure and renal function

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Weak P-glycoprotein inhibitor; may minimally increase tenofovir levels, though clinical impact is negligible
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance necessary, but counsel moderation; monitor for increased adverse effects if large quantities consumed

caution_foods.name: High-phosphate foods (dairy, nuts, seeds) in excess
caution_foods.mechanism: Tenofovir causes hypophosphatemia; excessive dietary restriction may worsen phosphate depletion in susceptible patients
caution_foods.action: Maintain balanced phosphate intake; renal function and electrolytes typically determine dietary need rather than restriction

monitoring_notes: Baseline and periodic monitoring of serum creatinine, phosphate, calcium, and urinalysis is essential to detect early renal dysfunction. Counsel patients on adequate hydration (2-3L daily) and annual renal function assessment, particularly in those with pre-existing kidney disease, diabetes, or hypertension.
